## Overview

This note summarises the HTTP status codes the OpenAlex API returns and how
`openalexPro` handles each of them. All requests go through the internal
`api_call()`. Sources: [Error Handling](https://help.openalex.org/api/errors/)
and [Authentication](https://help.openalex.org/api/authentication/).

Error responses are JSON with two fields, `error` (a short label) and `message`
(an explanation). OQL queries report problems as
`{"validation": {"errors": [{"type", "message", "position"}]}}` instead.
`openalexPro` includes this explanation in the R error. Error responses cost no
credits.

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning | `openalexPro` |
|--------|---------|---------------|
| 200 | Success | Returns the response |
| 301 | Entity was merged into another one | Follows the redirect |
| 400 | Bad request: invalid filter, parameter or OQL syntax | Stops; the error shows OpenAlex's message |
| 403 | No access to the resource | Stops; the error shows OpenAlex's message |
| 404 | Entity does not exist (also: a collection you cannot read) | Stops; the error shows OpenAlex's message |
| 429 | More than 100 requests per second | Retries with exponential backoff (up to 10 attempts) |
| 429 | Daily budget used up, or `not_enough_credits` (an OQL query costs more than is left) | Stops at once; the error says when the budget resets |
| 500, 502, 503, 504 | Temporary server problem | Retries with exponential backoff (up to 10 attempts) |

Network failures (dropped connections, curl errors) are retried like the
temporary server errors, and a transfer that stalls (less than 1 byte/s for
120 seconds) is aborted and retried.

## Budgets and rate limits

OpenAlex charges each call against a daily budget, which resets at midnight
UTC:

- without an API key: $0.10 per day
- with a free API key: $1 per day
- paid plans and prepaid usage raise this further

Typical costs: a single-entity lookup (`/works/W123`) is free, a filter (list)
query costs $0.0001, a search (`search`, `search.exact`, `search.semantic`)
costs $0.001, and a PDF download costs $0.01 (see
[Example costs](https://help.openalex.org/access/example-costs/)). Independent
of the budget, more than 100 requests per second return 429.

Every response carries these headers:

| Header | Content |
|--------|---------|
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Total daily budget |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | What is left for today |
| `X-RateLimit-Credits-Used` | Cost of this request (0 for errors) |
| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Seconds until the reset (midnight UTC) |

`pro_rate_limit_status()` shows the current budget, usage and reset time.

## API key instead of the polite pool

Before February 2026, adding a contact email (`mailto=`) placed requests in a
faster "polite pool". OpenAlex now ignores `mailto`; use a free API key
instead. `openalexPro` reads it with `pro_api_key()`, from the option
`openalexPro$api_key` or the environment variable `openalexPro.api_key`, and
sends it with every request.
